title: Integral split representation group and its canonical scalar-extension map
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $A$ a unital associative $K$-algebra. A finite-dimensional left $A$-module is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$ with a unital $K$-algebra homomorphism $A\to\operatorname{End}_K(V)$. Its isomorphisms are invertible $K$-linear maps intertwining the actions. Define $R_K(A)$ to be the free abelian group on such modules, modulo the subgroup generated by $[V]-[W]$ for isomorphic modules and $[W]-[U]-[V]$ whenever $W$ is isomorphic as an $A$-module to $U\oplus V$. For a field extension $L/K$, form $A_L=L\otimes_K A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with multiplication $(l\otimes a)(m\otimes b)=lm\otimes ab$. The extended module is $L\otimes_K V$, with $(l\otimes a)(m\otimes v)=lm\otimes av$. Extension of scalars sends the relation subgroup into the relation subgroup, and hence defines the canonical homomorphism $s_{L/K}:R_K(A)\to R_L(A_L)$ carrying $[V]$ to $[L\otimes_K V]$. The construction may use modules with underlying types in any universe at least as large as both coefficient fields; every finite-dimensional isomorphism class has a representative there.
